pr_body:
### Motivation and Context
- Fixes #15300
- Fixes #15389
- Fixes #15369
- Fixes #15214
- Fixes #15031
- Adds support for "Apple Developer" and "Apple Distribution" provision profiles to `sigh` (and `match`)

### Description

❗Enterprise accounts have access to "Apple Development" but not "Apple Distribution"

#### Sigh
- Concatenates with `Spaceship.certificate.apple_development.all` or `Spaceship.certificate.apple_distribution.all` in `Sigh::Runner` in the method for `certificates_for_profile_and_platform`. This method is used for determining provisioning profiles are available  for a specific platform and development type.
- Before this PR, a profile could not be generated with the new certificate types.

#### Cert
- Will create certs using `Spaceship.certificate.apple_development.all` or `Spaceship.certificate.apple_distribution.all` if `generate_apple_certs` param is `true. This param will default to `true` if Xcode 11 is being used

#### Match
- Will forward `generate_apple_certs` from _match_ params into _cert_ params with same Xcode 11 default value
- Also fixes `match nuke` to detect the new cert types to 💣 

### Testing Steps

#### Before this PR
```sh
$ fastlane sigh -a <BUNDLE_ID> --force -i <CERT_ID>
...
WARN [2019-09-29 16:32:14.76]: No certificates for filter: Certificate ID: '<CERT_ID>'
```

#### After this PR
```sh
$ fastlane sigh -a <BUNDLE_ID> --force -i <CERT_ID>
...
WARN [2019-09-29 16:35:04.41]: Creating new provisioning profile for '<BUNDLE_ID>' with name '<BUNDLE_ID>' for 'ios' platform
WARN [2019-09-29 16:35:05.21]: Downloading provisioning profile...
```

comments:
It seems like this issue might be related to code signing :no_entry_sign:

Have you seen our new [Code Signing Troubleshooting Guide](https://docs.fastlane.tools/codesigning/getting-started/)? It will help you resolve the most common code signing issues :+1:

This appears to be because sigh [uses](https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane/blob/master/sigh/lib/sigh/runner.rb#L158)
```ruby
      when 'ios', 'tvos'
        if profile_type == Spaceship.provisioning_profile.Development
          certificates = Spaceship.certificate.development.all
```
and `Spaceship.certificate.development.all` in turn filters certs [using](https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane/blob/master/spaceship/lib/spaceship/portal/certificate.rb#L279)

```ruby
types = [CERTIFICATE_TYPE_IDS.key(self)]
```

thus returning _only_ the old-style "iOS Development" certs.

There's two general ways I see to fix this:

1) Update `Spaceship.certificate.development.all` and `Spaceship.certificate.mac_development.all` to also include `AppleDevelopment` certs.

2) Update `sigh` (and anywhere else that matters) to merge the list from `Spaceship.certificate.apple_development.all` into the certs list for development profiles.

... then repeat either for `AppleDistribution` certs as well.
